title: Grammar file
description: One grammar concept. Every part renders on a single lesson screen in the order given, so a file should cover one idea rather than several. Only the five presentational part types below are rendered — an exercise belongs in the exercise file, and anything else is silently dropped by the grammar renderer.

title.description: The screen heading, unless the lesson section overrides it.

sections.description: Parts of the explanation, rendered in order on one screen. A typical concept is text, then examples or a table, then a tip.

partTitle.description: Rendered as a sub-heading. Omit it when it would repeat the file title — the renderer skips a title identical to the screen's.

table.description: Two-column reference table. The first column renders bold, unless bothAudible is set.

bothAudible.description: Gives both columns a listen button instead of just the first, for letter-to-word or pair-to-pair phonetic tables where both sides are worth hearing.

tip.description: A callout for the thing learners get wrong.

externalLink.description: The closing reference of a grammar explanation. Renders as a sentence — 'Read more about the use of ser on Lingolia.' — with only the site name hyperlinked, so the reference reads as part of the teaching rather than a bare link hanging off the end. Put it last in sections.

topic.description: Completes the sentence 'Read more about ___ on Lingolia.' — a noun phrase, lower case, no trailing full stop.

site.description: The hyperlinked words. Defaults to Lingolia when omitted.

sections.title: Introducing Yourself
sections.content: Use the verb 'ser' to say who you are and where you are from.
Spanish usually omits the subject pronoun: 'Soy Carlos.', not 'Yo soy Carlos.'
